issues: Grader code defect — declared intensity tolerance is never enforced: in check_spectra_content of grader_code, `dint = abs(sint - rint)` is computed and folded into the passing message (worst_int), but unlike `dmz > MZ_ATOL` there is no `if dint > INTENSITY_ATOL: fail(...)` branch. Both check id `spectra_content`'s public requirement ('each normalized intensity within 1e-9 of the reference value') and the acceptance-rules text declare this comparison. Confirmed by the executed control `intensity-tolerance-out-of-bound` (probe shifted 137 intensities of spectrum 999 by exactly 2e-9): the grader PASSED with message 'max |dintensity|=2.000e-09' — i.e. the grader computed and printed the out-of-bounds difference without rejecting it (passed_control: false in the control ledger). Consequence: any intensity corruption inside [0.01-1e-9, 1.0+1e-9], including wholly wrong intensity values, is accepted by `spectra_content`; the intensity content of processed_spectra.json — which feeds the cosine scores — is effectively unenforced except for the range and max-is-1 rules. Fix: add the missing `dint > INTENSITY_ATOL` failure check and re-run all controls; the existing `intensity-within-tolerance` (4e-10) and `intensity-tolerance-out-of-bound` (2e-9) probes already calibrate both sides of the corrected boundary.

Check-description defect / failed controls — cross_output_consistency claims an identifier join it does not perform: the check's public requirement and acceptance-rule section 5 state that 'best_matches.csv rows carry the identifiers of the same matched spectrum index in processed_spectra.json (empty string where the spectrum's post-pipeline value is undefined)', but check_consistency in grader_code only verifies the diagonal-matches/retained-count equality across processed_spectra.json, peak_counts.csv and both npz matrices — it never reads the submission's best_matches.csv or any identifier field. This is why the executed controls `swap-spectrum-annotations` and `best-match-substitutions` recorded passed_control: false: their expected check_ids include `cross_output_consistency`, but that check passed while only `spectra_content`/`best_matches_ranked_lists` failed. Either implement the described identifier join inside `cross_output_consistency` or correct the check description and both probes' `check_ids` (identifiers are already verified reference-side). The failed control records remain failures until repaired and re-executed.

Cosmetic grader-message off-by-one: in check_best_matches, failure messages use the 0-based enumerate index r as the reported rank ('rank %d' % r, 'rank %d' % (query_index, measure, mmf, r, mi)), so a row with rank 2 is reported as 'rank 1' — observed in the executed best-match-substitutions control, where the probe edited branch A rank 2 but the grader's failure message cites 'rank 1: matched_smiles does not match the reference record of spectrum 1100'. Correct to r+1 so failure reports are accurate.
rationale: The task construction, reference derivation and submission-path semantics are sound, and most controls pass as expected, but the candidate cannot be accepted because the grader is missing an entire declared numerical comparison and two executed wrong-solution controls failed. (1) check_spectra_content never enforces the declared 1e-9 intensity-vs-reference comparison: the code computes `dint = abs(sint - rint)` and prints it in the passing message but, unlike the m/z comparison (`if dmz > MZ_ATOL: fail(...)`), contains no `if dint > INTENSITY_ATOL: fail(...)` branch. The executed `intensity-tolerance-out-of-bound` control proves the defect: shifting 137 intensities of spectrum 999 by exactly 2e-9 produced a PASS with message 'max |dintensity|=2.000e-09' (control record passed_control: false). A submission can therefore report wholly wrong normalized intensities anywhere inside [0.01-1e-9, 1.0+1e-9] (subject only to the range, max-is-1 and zero-vs-nonzero rules) and still pass spectra_content, so the peak-intensity content of processed_spectra.json — the input to the cosine scores — is unenforced; the check's own public requirement states 'each normalized intensity within 1e-9 of the reference value'. (2) The `cross_output_consistency` check's public requirement and acceptance-rules text claim that best_matches.csv rows are joined to the identifiers of the matched spectrum in processed_spectra.json, but check_consistency only verifies the diagonal-matches/retained-count identity and never inspects identifiers. This misdescription is the direct cause of the two other failed controls: `swap-spectrum-annotations` and `best-match-substitutions` listed `cross_output_consistency` among their expected failing check_ids, but that check passed while the reference-side identifier checks (spectra_content/best_matches_ranked_lists) caught the corruption. (3) Minor: check_best_matches reports ranks with a 0-based index in failure messages (probe edited rank 2; the grader message cited 'rank 1'). All three defects are repairable without changing the scientific question, the tolerances or the public contract: add `if dint > INTENSITY_ATOL: fail(...)` in check_spectra_content, implement (or remove from the description and probe annotations) the identifier join in check_consistency, and fix the rank message off-by-one, then re-run the full control suite including the three currently-failed probe controls. Everything else was verified from the supplied evidence: the derivation cross-validated its source-faithful rerun against the recorded reference exports (peaks/metadata exact for all 1267 spectra, modified cosine matrices max diff 0.0 with exact match counts, branch E rows validated); the independently executed solution and the oracle produced byte-identical four-file outputs at the recorded hashes; the misplaced-file control confirms the declared-path rule matches the controller artifact_interface; the misplaced/empty/missing/recomputed/alternative controls all behave as described; tolerance choices are grounded in measured data (minimum adjacent-score gap ~1.4e-4 vs the 1e-9 tolerance, boundary probes 5e-10/1e-8 for scores, 4e-10/2e-9 for intensities with both sides of each boundary exercised); no answer fixtures exist among installed distributions and dependency exclusions are empty; the solver receives only the raw MGF. Source coverage preserves every eligible scientific endpoint (both similarity families and all five ranked branches recovered by faithful rerun, plus before/after peak counts), with disclosures consistent with what is graded.

All eligible terminal scientific results of the notebook are retained: the processed library (metadata+peak pipelines) in processed_spectra.json; before/after per-spectrum peak counts (call-36-56, call-124) in peak_counts.csv; the all-pairs CosineGreedy scores/matches and ModifiedCosine scores/matches in similarity_scores.npz; and all five ranked best-match branches (queries 5 greedy unfiltered/min>=5, queries 5/11/97 modified min>=5) in best_matches.csv. Exclusions that remain are appropriately classified: matplotlib histograms (call-59-63, 127-131, 215-230) are presentation of quantities fully retained in peak_counts.csv; RDKit depictions (call-180-182, 247-249, 265-267) render SMILES already exported in best_matches.csv; pre-pipeline metadata spot checks (call-46-48, 50, 53, 121) and the precursor-mass inspection (call-253-255) are diagnostics for choosing the query indices; the pickle export (call-149-151) is serialization of the identical spectrums object retained as processed_spectra.json and is recorded as support rather than a redundancy claim. No invented analysis, no silent endpoint omission, no scope change relative to the source.
